main_text.p: Hæc igitur consistit in Spirituum & caloris nativi conservatione; Conservantur autem illa tum Spiratione, tum Pulsu.Spiratio.
Spiratio, est aëris inspirati motio. Estq; Insensilis, aut Sensilis.
Insensilis dicitur Respiratio, quæ fit in toto corpore per insensiles poros.
Sensilis dicitur Respiratio, qua aër per pulmones cordi inspiratur, & postmodum expiratur ad vitæ conservationem.Pulsus.
Pulsus est motus cordis & arteriarum, constans διαστολὴ καὶ συστολή, consequens actionem animæ circa generationem spirituum vitalium occupatæ, ut calor eventiletur & fuligines expellantur.
Αἰσθητικὴ facultas ex sentiendi principio orta, cognitione sensuum insequitur.Αἰσθη- τικὴ.
Appetens, unde APPETITUS est vis animæ sentientis, quâ sui conservandi causâ inclinatur & fertur animal in suum bonum, vel aversatur sibi malum, prout ipsi sensus judicaverint.Facultas appetitiva.

page.notes: The Greek words in the text (διαστολὴ καὶ συστολή and the marginal Αἰσθητικὴ) are copied from the scan and may contain small errors; the marginal Greek is hyphenated across two lines as printed. The main-text line "Insensilis" is read from the scan and may be "Infensilis". The catchword "tivus" ends the page and is continued at the head of the next page. The continuation line "tivus" is a catchword and is not repeated in the text; the last line "sensi-" is hyphenated and completes as "sensitivus".
